::: {#exr-miller-int-trig-substitution}
#### Substitution with a trigonometric integrand

Adapted from @problifesavercalc, Question 1.1.38.

Evaluate the integral:

$$\int_0^2 x\cos(3x^2)\,dx$$
:::

::: {#sol-miller-int-trig-substitution}
Let $u = 3x^2$. Then $du = 6x\,dx$, meaning $x\,dx = \frac{du}{6}$.

Limits:

- When $x = 0$: $u = 0$.
- When $x = 2$: $u = 3(2^2) = 12$.

Substitute:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\int_0^2 x\cos(3x^2)\,dx
&= \frac{1}{6}\int_0^{12} \cos u\,du \\
&= \frac{1}{6}\sb{\sin u}_0^{12} \\
&= \frac{\sin 12}{6}
\end{aligned}
$$
:::
